This alembic will be textured later with Substance Painter and used directly in the shot. Open the main character project and import the animated character specific for this shot. It is important to remember that the animated character should start from the A pose in same position as the character in the main character project. This saves refitting or repositioning the garment on the character which can take a lot of time. All that is needed after import is to reattach the pins to the new avatar. So the clothing does not stick to the hanging baggage. Simulate. Once happy with the results, export a PC2 cache for 3ds Max or Maya cache for Maya and plug into the MD driver and MD cloth setup in the last tutorial. This same method is used for the third shot and the final shot. For the final shot, the character needs to open up the tint flap and exit. Again, the animated character is added to the original tint project. The skin offset of the character for this shot is set to 12. The tint flap itself has a fabric thickness setting of 50. Because only the tint flap being opened is needed for the cloth simulation, the tint has been removed and made double-sided, and then exported from 3ds Max. Then it is imported as an added avatar to the main character project in Marvelous Designer. Both static friction and kinetic friction are again set to zero, so the clothes do not stick to the tint flap. Finally, to simulate the strong wind outside the tint, the wind controller is animated to reflect this. Set the wind strength to zero. In order to animate parameters of the wind controller, the key activate box must be checked beneath the strength setting. At frame 60, add a key to keep the wind at zero until then. At frame 230, change wind strength to 700 and add a key. This will cause the wind to gradually increase in strength as the character exits the tint and steps into the full force of the wind. All these settings for wind strength are the result of tests done previously to see how strong the wind should be. Simulate the garment and when happy with results, export a PC2 cache for use in 3ds Max or a Maya cache for use in Maya. Lastly, Marvelous Designer has recently added multiple wind controllers. These can be used to create many varied and interesting wind effects where desired. This hood is being animated by two wind controllers. Both are individually animated. In order to make an additional wind controller, right-click on it and select Duplicate. Remember when animating the attributes of the wind controller to make sure the appropriate key activate box is checked. This concludes part 3 of this series. Thanks for watching! I'll see you next time! Bye!
summary: # Cfx Workflow: Part 3 - Interactions & Animation Welcome to the Marvelous Designer in CFX Series. In Part 3, we will be looking at interactions between multiple simulations. ## Interaction with Hanging Baggage The character in the second and third shots moves aside some hanging baggage as he moves through the tent. In the last shot, the character opens the tent to walk outside. The interactions between the character and bags, and later with the tent flap, must be done in the following way to avoid changing the point count of the finished costume. Adding any cloth geometry will make the point caches not work with the completed setup we did in the last tutorial. These bags are meant to look filled with something, so use positive pressure on the bag patterns to puff them out. 1. **Bag Preparation**: - Select half of every bag, right-click, and choose "Solidify." - This helps maintain the bag's shape as the character moves them aside. - The bags have been pinned at the top to keep them hanging in place. Once this cluster of bags looks right, they can be copied and edited slightly to create a variety of bags. Rotate them and delete parts as desired. ## Importing Avatars After the bags are placed aesthetically from the camera's perspective, the character avatar and the inner structure of the tent avatar are imported. This is done separately, as the tent structure is an OBJ file. 1. **Avatar Import**: - Choose "Import Add" from the menu. - Set the avatar's skin offset to 9. - This offset provides space for when the clothes are simulated against the pre-simulated bags. Once the tags are kindled and the background is 3D, the colors will appear more realistic. After simulating and ensuring the results look good, export the bags as an Alembic file. This Alembic will be textured later using Substance Painter and used directly in the shot. ## Character Animation Open the main character project and import the animated character specific for this shot. It is essential to remember that the animated character should start from the A pose in the same position as the character in the main character project. This approach saves time on refitting or repositioning the garment on the character. After the import, all that is needed is to reattach the pins to the new avatar. Next, import the hanging baggage Alembic that was previously simulated. 1. **Frictions Settings**: - Again, use "Import, Add, Alembic" for this. - Set both static and kinetic friction to zero to prevent the clothing from sticking to the hanging baggage. Simulate the garment. Once satisfied with the results, export a PC2 cache for 3ds Max or a Maya cache for use in Maya, and plug it into the MD driver and MD cloth setup from the last tutorial. This same method is applied for the third shot and the final shot. ## Final Shot - Tent Flap Interaction In the final shot, the character needs to open the tent flap and exit. Again, add the animated character to the original tent project. The skin offset of the character for this shot is set to 12. 1. **Tent Flap Settings**: - The tent flap itself has a fabric thickness setting of 50. - Since only the tent flap being opened is necessary for the cloth simulation, the tent has been removed and made double-sided, then exported from 3ds Max. - Import this as an added avatar to the main character project in Marvelous Designer. Both static and kinetic friction should again be set to zero to prevent the clothes from sticking to the tent flap. ## Simulating Wind Effects Finally, to simulate the strong wind outside the tent, the wind controller is animated to reflect this. 1. **Wind Controller Setup**: - Set the wind strength to zero. - To animate parameters of the wind controller, ensure the key activate box is checked beneath the strength setting. - At frame 60, add a key to maintain the wind at zero until then. - At frame 230, change the wind strength to 700 and add a key. This will cause the wind to gradually increase in strength as the character exits the tent and steps into the full force of the wind. All these settings for wind strength are based on tests conducted previously to establish the appropriate wind intensity. Simulate the garment, and when satisfied with the results, export a PC2 cache for use in 3ds Max or a Maya cache for use in Maya. ## Advanced Wind Effects Lastly, Marvelous Designer has recently added multiple wind controllers, which can be used to create various and interesting wind effects where desired. 1. **Animating Multiple Wind Controllers**: - The hood is being animated by two wind controllers, both of which are individually animated. - To create an additional wind controller, right-click on it and select "Duplicate." - Remember to ensure the appropriate key activate box is checked when animating the attributes of the wind controller. This concludes Part 3 of the series. Thanks for watching! I'll see you next time. Bye!
